fields.title: Reservations keeps no state of its own

sections.Context: The reserve-and-pay flow takes a borrower through several pages before a hold exists, and it runs on the shared branch terminals as well as on a borrower's own device. Something has to decide where a reservation lives between the first page and the confirmed hold. The answer reaches two repositories: `platform`, where [svc-reservations](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b57eb9eed273437f83f683bd6e18864d2b6b3372/examples/library/services/reservations.md) hosts the flow, and `lending`, where [svc-lending](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/b57eb9eed273437f83f683bd6e18864d2b6b3372/examples/library/services/lending.md) owns every hold in the legacy database.
sections.Decision:
Reservations keeps no state of its own. Wizard state before confirmation is ephemeral, and passes from page to page through the flow. The only durable write is the provisional hold the service creates through the lending API when the borrower confirms, and that hold's reference is what a card payment returns against.

Resuming a half-finished reservation in a later session is deliberately not supported.
sections.Consequences:
* **A borrower who leaves part-way starts again.** Nothing is kept for a later session, on any device.
* **The service runs no database, no storage account and no connection string.** There is nothing of its own to back
  up, migrate or hold to a retention period.
* **The lending API is the one owner of every hold.** A change to what a hold records is a change in `lending`, never a
  second copy in `platform`.
* **A payment taken after the borrower closes the browser leaves its hold provisional.** The flow keeps nothing that
  could finish the hold once the borrower has gone, and nothing reconciles the payment with the hold.
